On a typical day from October 1–7, 2026, you slept about **455 minutes (7 hours 35 minutes)**, counting naps. That figure comes from October 2, the only day in that range with sleep data. Its main sleep was 420 minutes, so the remaining 35 minutes were naps.

So **1 of the 7 days has sleep data** (about 14% coverage). The other six days have no sleep records, which I haven't counted as zero. With only one day, there's no meaningful typical-day average.

The sparse coverage may reflect what's been imported rather than your actual sleep. Locally, the only sleep record in the database is from Google, and there's no Fitbit sleep data at all. If you expect more nights for this week, I can run a sync to pull in recent records.
